'''Quests''' are stories that can be started in ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds''. They are provided by [[non-player character]]s such as the [[Wise Old Man]]. 

==List of quests==

===Primary===
'''Primary quests''' are quests that tells the main narrative of ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' and help players explore the entirety of the game (such as opening up new areas/regions). It is '''important to note''' that each subsequent quest in the narrative requires completion of the previous quest before starting the next.

===Secondary===
'''Secondary quests''' are quests that tell more personalized stories within the continent of Ashenfall. These quests help the player learn about new mechanics that hadn't been explored before, grant access to new mechanics, or unlock recipes for special items that help improve combative gameplay. It is ''important to note'' that unless you have either started a new or finished a primary quest (like finishing Dragon Slayer to start Withering Heights), you will be unable to start certain region-specific secondary quests.

=== Tertiary ===
'''Tertiary quests''' are quests that are that can be activated when doing a [[Quests#Primary|primary quest]]. These quests are not like '''secondary''' '''quests''', where they can be done by speaking to any NPC that would give it, they are instead triggered by doing a primary quest that has a list of tertiary quests for you to do. The first quest to feature this is [[Icthlarin's Little Helper]].

== Trivia ==

*Despite the news post calling them '''Spectral Chinchompas''' and '''The Collector Calling''', the quests' names in-game are different.
** The same has happened with [[A Room With A Garou]], the trailer and news post calls it "A Room With Garou"
*During the '''Early Access''' stage of the game, players that had completed a primary quest would automatically start the next one upon logging in.
*Through bugs or usage of mods, it is possible for players to start a different primary quest even if the previous one was not completed.
**This would break the game, causing progress to halt and forcing players to be stuck.
